correctness.rationale: Every nontrivial Lyndon subsequence of 0^a1^b0^c1^d has two or four alternating nonempty runs. A four-run word 0^i1^j0^k1^l is Lyndon iff i>k or i=k,j<l, by comparing the suffix starting at the second zero run. Minimizing deletions over this criterion and the two-run option gives D=min(b,max(0,c-a+1_{b>=d})); equality cases a=c,b=d and c=1 are addressed. Positive-composition counting splits b<d vs b>=d, yields displayed exact generating functions; simplex Dirichlet integral gives P(D/n>t)=(1/2)(1-2t)^3 for 0<t<1/2, atom 1/2 at zero, and mean length 15n/16+O(1).
risks: Uniform random positive-composition law, not Bernoulli random strings.
Finite enumerations are corroborative, not proof for arbitrary lengths.

value.rationale: Four alternating binary runs are the first family with a genuine choice between retaining both one-runs and discarding an interior run, and so are a natural minimal nontrivial case of the established longest-Lyndon-subsequence problem. Exact constant-time deficiency, entire rational distribution and nondegenerate limit with an atom give reusable precise information not mechanically obtained from a general individual-word algorithm.
risks: Restricted to four runs, fixed order, positive lengths; general sequences not classified.
